title: A three-branch union whose two array elements take DIFFERENT branches - now resolved
rationale: The shape a three-branch union exists FOR, and a different mechanism from its sibling row. Because one element takes the record branch and the other the string branch, the flattener emits BOTH a bare items_meta column and an items_meta_src child column. That means the array node has a flat column for the field AND a child node for it, so element 0 must resolve to the record while element 1 must resolve to the string - from the same two columns, distinguished only by index. It is the arity-3 mirror of avro-array-of-records-nullable-nested-record-shadowed's flat-column-shadows-child-column mechanism, and the sibling fixture cannot reach it. THIS ROW WAS DEFECT UNTIL 2.1.0 AND IS NOW THE CONTROL FOR ITS OWN REPAIR: the residual fault was never in the reconstructor at all. It was MapFlattener emitting items_meta MISALIGNED, putting element 1's value at index 0. Once the flattener writes array-element columns by index, the reconstructor already had everything it needed.
catchesBugClass: A union resolver that decides once per FIELD instead of once per ELEMENT. Any implementation that reads the child node's column set and commits to one branch for the whole array gets one of the two elements wrong here, and gets it wrong silently. It now ALSO catches a regression in the flattener's positional contract: if array-element columns ever go back to being appended and tail-padded, element 1's scalar lands at index 0 again and this row goes straight back to throwing at items[1].meta.
cannotCatch: It does not prove the resolver is right when both columns are populated for the SAME element, which is a genuinely contradictory input the flattener cannot produce from a well-formed document. It also cannot express ragged columns, for the same reason no corpus row can. It cannot distinguish a positional hole from a value that was genuinely written as null - no marker exists for that, and adding one would be a format change.

predicted.detail: LOSSLESS since 2.1.0. The id is deliberately left defect-shaped so the history stays legible; precedent is avro-array-element-multi-branch-union-dropped. Element 0 resolves to the record branch via the index-aware nested-record helper, and element 1 falls past the failing record branch to the type-directed STRING branch, so meta comes back as the record {src: web} and as the string 'plain' respectively. What changed is UPSTREAM: MapFlattener now writes each array-element column by INDEX instead of appending and tail-padding, so items_meta is [null, plain] rather than [plain, null]. Before that, element 1's string sat at index 0 and the reconstructor threw ReconstructionException 'Could not match any union type at: items[1].meta'.
